title: queue-bleed-coalescence-scratch-vivian-ortega
content:
Goal: explore 'queue bleed' — small-request leak-through causing tail amplification — and evaluate a lightweight request coalescing policy for mixed-priority workloads (interactive short requests + long-generative jobs).

Background/Why: we see P99 inflate when a small number of tiny low-priority requests slip past batching boundaries and force kernel wakeups. Hypothesis: a short-window coalescer at the front of the worker (10-30ms) plus preferential micro-batches for high-priority tiny requests can reduce tail without harming throughput for long requests.

Setup (local GCP dev pool):
- Node: n1-standard-16 + 1xA10G (dev cluster slice)
- Serving binary: rdinfr-runtime v1.14.0-alpha (kernel wakeup sampling enabled)
- Model: distilled-xxl (approx 7B, 2048 context) quantized int8 path
- Traffic generator: custom Go harness + wrk2 for background long requests
- Workload mix: 80% long (tokens ~1k, p50 latency baseline 420ms), 20% tiny (tokens ~8, target p50 <20ms)
- Priority: tiny requests marked high_priority=true (should get fast path)
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latencies per class, throughput (RPS), batching efficiency (avg batch size), kernel wakeups/sec, CPU context switches, KV cache hit ratio

Experiment matrix:
1) baseline (no coalescer, current batching window 8ms)
2) soft-coalesce: front-coalescer window 12ms for high_priority-only, fallthrough to normal batching for others
3) hard-coalesce: global front-coalescer window 25ms, but allow immediate dispatch if batch size >=8 or max_wait reached
4) hybrid: high_priority immediate micro-batches (max size 4), global coalescer 15ms for low-priority

Commands run (abridged):
- start harness: ./bench-gen -cfg tiny:400rps:tokens=8:prio=high long:1600rps:tokens=1000:prio=low -mix 20:80 -duration 12m | tee run.log
- collect traces: ./trace-capture --out traces/run-XX.json --sample 0.02
- runtime flags: --coalesce-window-ms=12 --coalesce-only-high=true

Crude results (median of three runs, numbers are ms where applicable):
- baseline: tiny p50=18, p90=42, p99=210; long p50=425, p90=560, p99=980; throughput steady at 2300 rps; avg batch size=5.1; wakeups/sec=320
- soft-coalesce: tiny p50=14, p90=28, p99=72; long p50=430, p90=570, p99=990; throughput 2280 rps; avg batch size=5.4; wakeups/sec=220
- hard-coalesce: tiny p50=16, p90=34, p99=150; long p50=440, p90=590, p99=1010; throughput 2250 rps; avg batch size=6.0; wakeups/sec=160
- hybrid: tiny p50=12, p90=22, p99=45; long p50=438, p90=575, p99=995; throughput 2290 rps; avg batch tiny=3.2 overall batch=5.6; wakeups/sec=180

Observations/notes: 
- The large p99 for tiny requests in baseline appears correlated with sporadic kernel wakeups coincident with large long-request batches (trace sample shows tiny requests sometimes get delayed by 1+ batch cycle).
- Soft-coalesce (high-priority-only) gives a big reduction in tiny p99 with minimal throughput impact. Kernel wakeups/sec dropped ~30% and batch size barely changed. This supports the hypothesis that protecting tiny high-priority requests is low-cost.
- Hard global coalescing reduces wakeups more but increases variability for tiny requests (p99 still high vs soft-coalesce) — likely because low-priority accumulation increases chance of long-request preemption. 
- Hybrid is the best tradeoff in this matrix: explicit micro-batches for high-priority tiny traffic + modest global coalescing for low-priority keeps tiny tails low and throughput near baseline.

Quick root-cause trace snippet (hand transcription):
- tiny request A arrives at t=3.510s -> queued
- long batch B wakeup at t=3.516s -> consumes slot and triggers dispatch
- tiny A misses this batch, waits 8ms -> collided with background kernel scheduling -> p99 spike at t=3.530s
- coalescer prevented A from entering the dispatch window and instead created a micro-batch at t=3.522s -> tiny latency reduced to 12ms

Metrics to double-check (next pass):
- per-thread wakeup distribution (hot threads causing most wakeups)
- GC/allocator stalls correlation with tiny p99 (heap compaction on worker?)
- effect on KV cache reuse: micro-batches might reduce cache reuse for tiny seqs, check hits by token position
- GPU kernel launch latency histogram by batch size

Edge cases / risks noticed:
- Too-aggressive coalescing can increase end-to-end latency for low-priority bulk jobs; we must preserve SLOs for those customers.
- Micro-batches increase number of small kernel launches; need to evaluate GPU power/thermal implications at scale.
- If high-priority traffic bursts suddenly (10x), micro-batcher could create backpressure that affects scheduling; add backoff heuristics.

Implementation ideas (quick):
- Add dynamic coalesce window: target small-window when tiny traffic fraction < 30%, expand if backlog grows beyond threshold
- Priority-aware batching: form micro-batches for high_priority requests and prefer in-worker scheduling for <8 token requests
- Kernel hinting: annotate micro-batches to use "small-kernel" codepath that avoids heavy setup and tries to piggyback on existing CUDA contexts

Next experiments:
- Run hybrid config across 3-node heterogeneous cluster (mix of A100/A10) to verify kernel launch costs at scale (2025-03-03)
- Stress test: sudden 10x spike of tiny high_priority traffic for 30s to observe scheduler backoff behavior (2025-03-05)
- Add GC/allocator profiling during runs and retest to identify user-land stalls (2025-03-07)

Notes to self: save traces, grep for wakeup counts per tid, and compare p99 tails per GOM worker. Reach out to Luca for kernel-launch histograms and to Asha for infra-level thermal logging.

Raw artifacts: run logs in /tmp/bench-runs/queue-bleed/2025-02-18-*.log; traces in s3://rd-infr-dev/traces/queue-bleed/; toy patch at github PR linked above.

Conclusions (short): a small, priority-scoped front coalescer + micro-batching for tiny interactive requests cuts their tail substantially with negligible effect on overall throughput. Hybrid approach looks promising for productizing.

TODOs (short):

- [ ] Add dynamic coalesce window prototype in runtime repo
- [ ] Draft short playbook for SRE on coalescer tuning (can be ops-runbook)

End of scratchpad.
